issues.title: Missing braces in for loop
issues.description: The rule requires all control flow statements (if, else, for, foreach, while, do-while) to use curly braces even for single-line bodies, but the inner for loop omits curly braces
issues.rule_name: Use Curly Braces for All Control Flow Statements
issues.categorize_rationale: Missing braces in a for loop is a formatting/lint preference with no runtime impact.

issues.title: Inverted renderer type check prevents circuit restart
issues.description: The condition checking for different renderer types has been inverted from `!==` to `===`. This causes the function to throw an error when the SAME renderer type tries to re-enable JS root components (e.g., during circuit restart), which is the exact scenario that should be allowed. The original intent was to throw an error only when a DIFFERENT renderer type attempts to enable root components. This bug breaks circuit restart functionality, causing applications to fail when users reconnect after a circuit disconnect.
issues.categorize_rationale: Inverted condition breaks circuit restart, causing application failure on reconnect.

issues.title: Missing parameter update causes stale data on circuit restart
issues.description: The assignment `jsComponentParametersByIdentifier = jsComponentParameters;` has been removed from the re-enabling logic. When a circuit restarts and `enableJSRootComponents` is called again with new parameters, the global `jsComponentParametersByIdentifier` is not updated. This causes the application to continue using stale parameters from the previous circuit. The `DynamicRootComponent` class constructor and methods rely on `jsComponentParametersByIdentifier` to retrieve component parameter definitions, so they will operate with outdated metadata after a circuit restart.
issues.categorize_rationale: Missing parameter update causes stale data, leading to incorrect behavior after circuit restart.

issues.title: Test method missing Arrange/Act/Assert comments
issues.description: The added test method does not contain explicit '// Arrange', '// Act', and '// Assert' (or '// Act & Assert') comments to delineate the AAA phases, violating the required test structure convention.
issues.rule_name: Test Methods Must Use Arrange-Act-Assert Pattern with Comments
issues.categorize_rationale: Missing AAA comments is a test structure convention violation with no runtime impact.

issues.title: Tailwind classes in incorrect order
issues.description: Tailwind utility classes must follow standard ordering: layout, positioning, sizing, spacing (margin before padding), typography, visual effects. The classes have padding (pr-2) before margin (mt-[-16px]), which violates this convention.
issues.problematic_code_snippet: <div className='pr-2 mt-[-16px]'>
issues.rule_name: Tailwind CSS Classes Must Follow Standard Ordering
issues.categorize_rationale: Tailwind class ordering is a formatting convention with no runtime impact.

issues.title: Missing optional chaining causes runtime error when openForm is undefined
issues.description: The code accesses `openForm.in_reply_to_snippet` without optional chaining, but openForm can be undefined when rendering certain forms (like the main comment form). The original code correctly used `openForm?.in_reply_to_snippet` with optional chaining. This will cause a "Cannot read property 'in_reply_to_snippet' of undefined" runtime error when the FormWrapper is rendered without an openForm prop, crashing the component.
issues.categorize_rationale: Missing optional chaining causes a runtime crash when openForm is undefined.

issues.title: Editor editability incorrectly depends on member expertise instead of name
issues.description: The Form component determines whether the editor should be editable by checking `member?.expertise` instead of `memberName` (which is derived from `member?.name`). According to the comment and the original logic, the editor should be disabled only when the member doesn't have a name or when submitting. Expertise is optional metadata, but name is required for posting. This bug prevents users without expertise from typing in the comment editor, even though they have a valid name and should be allowed to comment.
issues.categorize_rationale: Incorrect condition prevents users without expertise from editing, breaking expected behavior.

issues.title: Reply threading broken for nested comments due to incorrect in_reply_to_id
issues.description: The submit function uses `parent.id` as `in_reply_to_id` instead of `openForm.in_reply_to_id`. For nested replies (replying to a reply), these values differ: `openForm.in_reply_to_id` points to the specific comment being replied to, while `parent.id` points to the top-level parent comment. Using `parent.id` breaks the reply chain, causing nested replies to be incorrectly threaded to the wrong comment. This destroys the conversation hierarchy and makes it impossible to track which comment a user is actually replying to in multi-level discussions.
issues.categorize_rationale: Using parent.id instead of openForm.in_reply_to_id breaks nested reply threading, destroying conversation hierarchy.

issues.title: JSX props ordered incorrectly
issues.description: The rule requires JSX props to be ordered with regular props before the children prop. In the FrameworkContext.Provider component, the children prop appears before the value prop, violating the standard ordering convention where regular props should come before children.
issues.problematic_code_snippet: <FrameworkContext.Provider children={children} value={props} />
issues.rule_name: React Components Must Sort JSX Props in Standard Order
issues.categorize_rationale: JSX prop ordering is a stylistic convention with no runtime impact.

issues.title: Incorrect version suffix order in endpoint URL construction
issues.description: The frontend code constructs Tinybird endpoint URLs with the version prefix in reverse order compared to the backend. The frontend builds URLs as `v2_api_kpis` (version first) while the backend expects `api_kpis_v2` (version last). This mismatch causes the frontend to call non-existent endpoints when the version config is set, resulting in failed API calls and missing analytics data. The comment correctly describes the pattern as 'api_kpis_v2' but the implementation reverses this to `${config.version}_${endpointName}`.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
// Append version suffix if provided (e.g., "v2" -> "api_kpis_v2")
const finalEndpointName = config.version ? `${config.version}_${endpointName}` : endpointName;
issues.categorize_rationale: Incorrect URL construction causes API calls to fail, breaking analytics data retrieval.

issues.title: Missing source parameter in Tinybird API request
issues.description: The fetchRawTopContentData method removes the critical logic that passes the `source` filter parameter to the Tinybird API. While the method still handles `options.source` validation (including empty strings for 'Direct' traffic) at lines 105-108 in the comment, it no longer assigns it to `tinybirdOptions.source`. This means source-based filtering will silently fail—the API endpoint will be called without the source parameter, returning unfiltered results instead of data filtered by the requested traffic source.
issues.categorize_rationale: Missing source parameter causes silent failure of source-based filtering, returning incorrect data.

issues.title: Version suffix applied in local development mode, breaking local Tinybird instances
issues.description: The PR removes the critical `!localEnabled` check that previously prevented version suffixes from being applied when running against local Tinybird instances. The old code only applied versioning in production (`options.tbVersion && !localEnabled`), but the new code always applies versioning when configured (`statsConfig?.version`), regardless of whether local mode is enabled. This breaks local development because local Tinybird instances typically only have base endpoint versions (e.g., `api_kpis`), not the v2 variants (e.g., `api_kpis_v2`), causing 404 errors when developers try to use local Tinybird for testing. The corresponding test 'ignores tbVersion when local is enabled' was also removed, confirming this behavior change was intentional but problematic.
issues.categorize_rationale: Removing local check breaks local development by causing 404 errors on Tinybird endpoints.

issues.title: Strict mode disabled in TypeScript config
issues.description: The rule requires TypeScript configuration files to have 'strict' set to true in compilerOptions, but it was set to false
issues.rule_name: TypeScript Files Must Enable Strict Type Checking
issues.categorize_rationale: Strict mode disabled reduces type safety and can mask bugs, but is not immediately breaking.

issues.title: Missing error handling in Bluesky enable function leaves UI in perpetual loading state
issues.description: The handleEnable function removes the try-catch block that was wrapping the enableBlueskyMutation call. When the API call fails (network error, server error, etc.), the loading state is never reset to false, leaving the user stuck with a spinning loader and no way to retry. This is inconsistent with the handleDisable function which properly handles errors. The bug causes a poor user experience where users must refresh the page to recover from any API failure.
issues.categorize_rationale: Missing error handling causes perpetual loading state, blocking user recovery.

issues.title: Polling logic performs one extra retry attempt beyond configured maximum
issues.description: The confirmation polling interval increments the retry counter after checking if the limit is reached, combined with changing the condition from `>` to `>=`. This creates an off-by-one error where the system will actually make 13 API calls (retries 0-12) instead of the intended 12 calls defined by MAX_CONFIRMATION_RETRIES. The counter starts at 0, gets incremented to 12, makes a call, then on the next iteration checks if 12 >= 12 and only then stops. This wastes API resources and delays the timeout error message by one additional polling interval (5 seconds).
issues.categorize_rationale: Off-by-one error causes extra API call and delays timeout, wasting resources.

issues.title: Missing query invalidation after Bluesky handle confirmation causes stale following list
issues.description: The confirmBlueskyHandle mutation successfully updates the account cache but fails to invalidate the accountFollows query. When Bluesky is enabled via Bridgy Fed, the account automatically follows the brid.gy account. Both enableBluesky and disableBluesky mutations properly invalidate QUERY_KEYS.accountFollows('index', 'following') to refresh this list, but confirmBlueskyHandle does not. This means after the handle is confirmed, the UI won't show the brid.gy follow relationship until the user manually refreshes the page or navigates away and back. This is inconsistent with the established pattern in the codebase and creates a confusing user experience where the integration appears incomplete.
issues.categorize_rationale: Missing query invalidation leads to stale UI data, inconsistent with other mutations.

issues.title: Missing semicolon after type alias declaration
issues.description: The `BlueskyDetails` type alias declaration is not terminated with a semicolon, relying on ASI. The codebase rule requires explicit semicolons at the end of statements.
issues.rule_name: Rule 19: Code Must Always Use Semicolons
issues.categorize_rationale: Missing semicolon is a formatting violation with no runtime impact.

issues.title: JSX attribute uses double-quoted string literals
issues.description: In this TSX file, the JSX attribute values for `className`, `href`, `rel`, and `target` are written using double quotes, violating the rule requiring single quotes for string literals in JS/TS files.
issues.problematic_code_snippet: Your social web profile is now connected to Bluesky, via Bridgy Fed. Posts are automatically synced after a short delay to complete activation.
issues.rule_name: Rule 18: Code Must Use Single Quotes for Strings
issues.categorize_rationale: Double quotes used instead of single quotes, violates style rule.

issues.title: Test file separated from component
issues.description: The rule requires that for every React component file component.tsx, the test file component.test.tsx exists in the same directory. However, the test file schema-form-input-array-list.test.tsx was placed in a __tests__ subdirectory instead of being co-located with schema-form-input-array-list.tsx.
issues.rule_name: React Component Test Files Must Be Co-Located
issues.categorize_rationale: Test file not co-located with component violates project convention.

issues.title: Drag-and-drop reordering swaps source and target indices
issues.description: The handleDragEnd function passes arguments to moveItem in the wrong order - it calls moveItem(newIndex, oldIndex) instead of moveItem(oldIndex, newIndex). This causes drag-and-drop operations to place items in the opposite position from where they're dropped. For example, dragging an item from index 2 to index 0 will incorrectly move the item at index 0 to index 2 instead, creating confusing and incorrect reordering behavior for users.
issues.categorize_rationale: Incorrect argument order causes opposite reordering behavior.

issues.title: Prefix items incorrectly included in sortable context
issues.description: The sortableKeys array is constructed from all localKeyedValues instead of excluding prefix items. The code removed the .slice(prefixItemsCount) operation, meaning prefix items (which should have fixed positions and not be draggable) are now included in the SortableContext. This allows prefix items to be moved via drag-and-drop, violating the constraint that prefix items must remain in their fixed positions and breaking the schema's structural requirements.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
// Get the keys of items that can be dragged (non-prefix items)
const sortableKeys = localKeyedValues.map((item) => item.key);
issues.categorize_rationale: Prefix items incorrectly included in sortable context, violating fixed positions.

issues.title: Unused local variable `prefixItemsCount` added
issues.description: `prefixItemsCount` is introduced but never referenced anywhere in the component. This leaves unused code in the codebase, violating the rule requiring unused items to be removed.
issues.rule_name: Unused Imports Must Be Automatically Removed
issues.categorize_rationale: Unused variable left in codebase, violates removal rule.

issues.title: Test file exceeds 800 lines
issues.description: The rule requires Python files in the backend (api/) to contain fewer than 800 lines of code, but this test file contains 1151 lines and should be split into multiple files

issues.rule_name: Python Backend Files Must Not Exceed 800 Lines
issues.categorize_rationale: File length limit is a code organization style rule, not a functional bug.

issues.title: Missing None-check allows invalid template render result to propagate
issues.description: The validation logic in `render_template` was modified to skip type checking when `rendered` is None. The original code correctly rejected None values with 'Template render result must be a string', but the new condition `if rendered is not None and not isinstance(rendered, str)` allows None to pass through and be returned. This will cause AttributeError exceptions downstream when code attempts to call string methods like `len()` on the None value, breaking template transformation workflows that depend on always receiving a valid string output.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
rendered = result.get("result")
        if rendered is not None and not isinstance(rendered, str):
            raise TemplateRenderError("Template render result must be a string.")
        return rendered
issues.categorize_rationale: Allowing None to propagate causes AttributeError downstream, breaking template transformation workflows.

issues.title: Incorrect code_executor parameter breaks dependency injection chain
issues.description: In the DifyNodeFactory constructor, the template renderer initialization passes the `code_executor` parameter instead of `self._code_executor`. Since `code_executor` is the optional constructor parameter that may be None, while `self._code_executor` is the resolved non-None instance (with fallback to CodeExecutor class), this breaks the dependency injection pattern. When users don't provide a code_executor, the renderer receives None instead of the default CodeExecutor, causing template rendering to fail with AttributeError when attempting to call `execute_workflow_code_template` on None.
issues.problematic_code_snippet: self._template_renderer = template_renderer or CodeExecutorJinja2TemplateRenderer(code_executor)
issues.categorize_rationale: Broken dependency injection causes template rendering to fail with AttributeError when no code_executor is provided.

issues.title: Variable scope error causes UnboundLocalError when template rendering succeeds
issues.description: The length validation check was moved inside the try block before the except clause, creating a critical variable scope issue. When `render_template()` succeeds, the `rendered` variable is assigned inside the try block. However, if the length check passes and no exception occurs, execution continues to the return statement outside the try-except block which references `rendered`. In Python, this creates an undefined variable scenario where `rendered` is only defined within the try block scope but accessed outside it, resulting in UnboundLocalError at runtime whenever template rendering succeeds without exceeding length limits.
issues.categorize_rationale: Variable scope bug causes UnboundLocalError at runtime whenever template rendering succeeds without exceeding length limits.

issues.title: New pytest test function missing type annotations
issues.description: Rule requires all Python function parameters and return values to be type-annotated. This newly added test function defines parameters (self, mock_execute, mock_graph, mock_graph_runtime_state, graph_init_params) without any type hints and has no return type annotation.
issues.rule_name: Python Functions Must Include Type Annotations
issues.categorize_rationale: Missing type annotations in test function is a style/lint issue with no runtime impact.

issues.title: New pytest test function missing type annotations
issues.description: Rule requires all Python function parameters and return values to be type-annotated. This newly added test function has unannotated parameters and no return type annotation.
issues.rule_name: Python Functions Must Include Type Annotations
issues.categorize_rationale: Missing type annotations in test function is a style/lint issue with no runtime impact.

issues.title: New pytest test function missing type annotations
issues.description: Rule requires all Python function parameters and return values to be type-annotated. This newly added test function has unannotated parameters (including a multi-line signature) and no return type annotation.
issues.rule_name: Python Functions Must Include Type Annotations
issues.categorize_rationale: Missing type annotations in test function is a style/lint issue with no runtime impact.

issues.title: Schema not regenerated after config change
issues.description: The rule requires that when source files like crates/tauri-utils/src/config.rs change, the corresponding generated schema files must be updated by running the schema generator build command. The code adds a new Flatpak bundle type to the BundleType enum without regenerating the schema files.
issues.rule_name: Generated Files Must Be Kept in Sync with Source Code
issues.categorize_rationale: Schema not regenerated leads to stale generated files, causing potential inconsistencies in code generation or validation.

issues.title: TOML parsing errors incorrectly wrapped as JSON errors
issues.description: The do_parse_toml function wraps TOML parsing errors as ConfigError::FormatJson instead of ConfigError::FormatToml. This causes misleading error messages when TOML configuration files fail to parse - users will be told there's a JSON parsing error when the actual issue is with TOML syntax. This breaks the error handling contract established by the ConfigError enum and will confuse developers trying to debug configuration issues. The error type conversion using serde_json::Error::custom also loses the detailed TOML error context that would normally be preserved in ConfigError::FormatToml.
issues.categorize_rationale: TOML parsing errors are misclassified as JSON errors, breaking error handling contract and misleading users.

issues.title: Case mismatch between BundleType serialization and deserialization for Flatpak
issues.description: The Display implementation for BundleType::Flatpak returns "Flatpak" with capital 'F', while the Deserialize implementation expects lowercase "flatpak". This creates a serialization round-trip bug where serializing a Flatpak bundle type and then deserializing it will fail. Any code that serializes bundle configurations to strings (for CLI output, config files, or API responses) and then attempts to parse them back will encounter deserialization errors. This inconsistency breaks the expected behavior that Display and Deserialize should be compatible with each other.
issues.categorize_rationale: Case mismatch causes serialization round-trip failure, leading to runtime errors when deserializing Flatpak bundle type.

issues.title: User-facing change added without a corresponding .changes entry
issues.description: This PR introduces a user-facing functionality change (adding a new `Flatpak` bundle type to the public config surface) but the diff does not include any new markdown change file under the `.changes/` directory (covector format) to document the change and version bump. Rule 13 requires such a change file for releasable functionality changes.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
+  /// The Flatpak bundle (.flatpak).
+  Flatpak,
issues.rule_name: Changes Requiring a Version Bump Must Include a Change File
issues.categorize_rationale: Missing .changes file for user-facing change violates project contribution rules, but does not affect code correctness.

issues.title: new_click method missing must_use attribute
issues.description: The new_click method returns a TrayIconEvent that represents an important event which should not be ignored. Factory methods that create event objects should be marked with #[must_use] to prevent accidentally creating an event without handling it, which could lead to silent logic errors.
issues.rule_name: Functions Returning Values Should Be Marked with must_use Where Appropriate
issues.categorize_rationale: Missing #[must_use] can lead to silent ignoring of events, causing logic errors.

issues.title: Inverted mouse button state mapping in tray icon event conversion
issues.description: The From implementation for converting tray_icon::MouseButtonState to MouseButtonState has the Up and Down states inverted. When a mouse button is released (Up) from the underlying tray_icon library, it's incorrectly mapped to Down in the Tauri TrayIconEvent, and vice versa. This will cause all tray icon click handlers to receive the opposite button state than what actually occurred, breaking event handling logic that depends on distinguishing between button press and release events. The new_click factory method added in this PR uses MouseButtonState::default() which is Up, but when real events are converted through this From implementation, the states will be backwards.
issues.categorize_rationale: Inverted mouse button state mapping breaks event handling logic.

issues.title: PatternJavascript struct gated behind isolation feature breaks brownfield pattern
issues.description: The PatternJavascript struct was moved behind a #[cfg(feature = "isolation")] gate, but this struct is used in webview initialization code (manager/webview.rs line 131) for all pattern types including Pattern::Brownfield. When the isolation feature is disabled, the PatternJavascript struct won't be defined, causing a compilation error in webview.rs when it tries to instantiate PatternJavascript for brownfield applications. This change in the derive attribute placement breaks the fundamental pattern system for non-isolation builds, preventing any Tauri application that doesn't use the isolation pattern from compiling.
issues.categorize_rationale: Compilation error in non-isolation builds due to incorrect feature gate.

issues.title: Config schema/source changed without corresponding generated artifacts update
issues.description: This PR modifies `crates/tauri-utils/src/config.rs` (a source file explicitly called out by Rule 14 as driving generated artifacts such as schemas). The diff does not include any updates to the corresponding generated outputs (e.g., regenerated JSON schemas / other generated artifacts that depend on this config). Under Rule 14, changes to this file require regenerating and committing the generated files to keep them in sync.
issues.rule_name: Generated Files Must Be Kept in Sync with Source Code
issues.categorize_rationale: Missing regenerated schema artifacts may cause validation inconsistencies.

issues.title: v1 config schema/source changed without corresponding generated artifacts update
issues.description: This PR also modifies `crates/tauri-utils/src/config_v1/mod.rs`, which is part of configuration/schema definitions. The diff does not include any regenerated artifacts that would normally need updating when configuration schema-related code changes (as required by Rule 14).
issues.rule_name: Generated Files Must Be Kept in Sync with Source Code
issues.categorize_rationale: Missing regenerated schema artifacts for v1 config may cause inconsistencies.

issues.title: Obfuscated SMTP class selection logic
issues.description: The rule requires code to maintain readable control flow and avoid clever hacks. The code uses a ternary expression to dynamically select and instantiate an SMTP class in a single line, making the logic harder to understand and maintain compared to a straightforward if-else structure.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
# Use ternary to select SMTP class based on TLS mode
smtp = (smtplib.SMTP_SSL if (self.use_tls and not self.opportunistic_tls) else smtplib.SMTP)(
    self.server, self.port, timeout=10, local_hostname=local_host
)
issues.rule_name: Python Backend Must Use Deterministic Control Flow
issues.categorize_rationale: Readability improvement for control flow, not a bug.

issues.title: Incorrect EHLO hostname parameter in opportunistic TLS mode
issues.description: When opportunistic TLS is enabled, the code passes `local_host` (which can be None or an empty string) to the EHLO command instead of using `self.server`. According to RFC 5321, the EHLO command should identify the client using its fully qualified domain name. The original code correctly used `self.server` as the EHLO identifier before this PR. This bug will cause SMTP servers that validate EHLO domains to reject the connection, especially when SMTP_LOCAL_HOSTNAME is not configured or is empty.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
assert smtp is not None
if self.use_tls and self.opportunistic_tls:
    smtp.ehlo(local_host)
    smtp.starttls()
    smtp.ehlo(local_host)
issues.categorize_rationale: Incorrect EHLO hostname causes SMTP connection rejection.

issues.title: Empty string fallback breaks SMTP local_hostname default behavior
issues.description: The code uses `dify_config.SMTP_LOCAL_HOSTNAME or ""` which converts None to an empty string. However, the smtplib library expects None (not an empty string) when no custom hostname is specified, allowing it to use the system's FQDN as a default. By providing an empty string instead of None, the SMTP connection will fail to properly identify itself during the HELO/EHLO handshake when SMTP_LOCAL_HOSTNAME is not configured. This breaks the intended fallback behavior and can cause mail delivery failures on servers that validate client hostnames.
issues.problematic_code_snippet: local_host = dify_config.SMTP_LOCAL_HOSTNAME or ""
issues.categorize_rationale: Empty string instead of None breaks hostname fallback, causing mail failures.

issues.title: Redundant empty string to None conversion defeats purpose of hostname override
issues.description: After converting None to empty string on line 25, the code then converts empty string back to None using `local_host or None` when passing to the SMTP constructor. This double conversion defeats the entire purpose of the SMTP_LOCAL_HOSTNAME feature. When a user explicitly sets SMTP_LOCAL_HOSTNAME to an empty string (perhaps to force default behavior), this logic will pass None to smtplib instead of respecting the user's configuration. The redundant `or None` should be removed, and the initial conversion to empty string is also problematic as explained in the previous issue.
issues.categorize_rationale: Double conversion defeats user-set hostname override, logic error.

issues.title: Inconsistent Chinese translation for 'Name' field across namespaces
issues.description: The PR updates the Chinese translation for 'Name' from '称呼' to '姓名' across multiple translation files to ensure consistency. However, this change creates a cross-namespace inconsistency issue. In ghost.json, line 31 shows 'Name' translated as '名字' (first name), while in portal.json line 117 it's translated as '名称' (generic name/title). This inconsistency will confuse Chinese users when they see different terminology for the same 'Name' field between email templates (using ghost namespace) and the portal UI (using portal namespace). The correct translation should be '姓名' (full name) consistently across both files as intended by the original PR.

    "Name": "名称",
    "Need more help? Contact support": "需要更多帮助？联系支持服务",
issues.categorize_rationale: Cross-namespace translation inconsistency causes user confusion for the same 'Name' field.

issues.title: Missing interpolation variable in newsletter unsubscribe message
issues.description: The translation for the key '{memberEmail} will no longer receive {newsletterName} newsletter.' in portal.json is missing the {newsletterName} interpolation variable. The Chinese translation only includes '{memberEmail}将不会再收到新闻信。' which omits the newsletter name placeholder. This means when users unsubscribe from a specific newsletter, they won't see which newsletter they're unsubscribing from, leading to confusion and potential accidental unsubscriptions. The translation should include both {memberEmail} and {newsletterName} variables to match the English source and maintain functional parity.

    "{discount}% discount": "{discount}% 折扣",

issues.categorize_rationale: Missing interpolation variable leads to incomplete unsubscribe message, causing user confusion and potential accidental unsubscriptions.

issues.title: Translation inconsistency for 'Enter your name' field across UI contexts
issues.description: The PR introduces an inconsistency in the Chinese translation for the 'Enter your name' input field. In portal.json line 71, it's translated as '输入您的名字' (enter your first name), which suggests only a first name is needed. However, based on the context of Ghost's user registration and profile system, and the fact that the 'Name' field itself should be '姓名' (full name), this creates a mismatch between what the label asks for ('名字' - first name) and what the system actually expects ('姓名' - full name). This can cause user confusion during registration and profile completion, potentially leading to incomplete or incorrectly formatted name entries.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
"Ends {offerEndDate}": "于{offerEndDate}结束",
    "Enter code above": "在上方输入验证码",
    "Enter your email address": "输入您的电子邮箱地址",
    "Enter your name": "输入您的名字",
    "Error": "错误",

issues.title: Deletion of comments.json breaks comments-ui build for Chinese locale
issues.description: The PR deletes ghost/i18n/locales/zh/comments.json, but this file is required by the comments-ui application build configuration. In apps/comments-ui/vite.config.mts line 56, the Vite build explicitly declares dynamicRequireTargets for comments.json across all SUPPORTED_LOCALES, including 'zh'. When the build system attempts to bundle the Chinese locale translations, it will fail because the required comments.json file no longer exists. This will break the build process for the comments-ui application or cause runtime failures when users try to view comments in Chinese.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
diff --git a/ghost/i18n/locales/zh/comments.json b/ghost/i18n/locales/zh/comments.json
deleted file mode 100644
index 1de6b189e6..0000000000
--- a/ghost/i18n/locales/zh/comments.json
+++ /dev/null
@@ -1,74 +0,0 @@
-{
-    "{amount} characters left": "还剩{amount}字",
-    "{amount} comments": "{amount}条评论",
issues.categorize_rationale: Deleting required file breaks the build for comments-ui application.
